I had some real basic ideas after binging some Familiar of Zero Fics. i challenge YOU to build a story off of these Ideas. Each Chapter is an idea, a spark. i want to see you ignite!
 
So a lot of people have mentioned how My use of AI in the Challenges series and their spinoffs leaves them half coherent and a bit crappy.I know. that's on purpose.if you see a story, that goes on a path you've never seen before, and its great, its emotional, its lore accurate, and it does everything you've ever wanted to see in a way you didn't know you wanted...
why would you want to try doing it yourself?
The challenges, My Sparks, are designed to catch the imagination. to make you say "huh, i never thought about that before." and inspire you to look at it, and give it a try yourself.
I find that is much easier when you are motivated.
by perhaps, it not being as good as it could be. by not exploring all the logical repercussions. or maybe by just sucking.
now you have an Idea, an example, and a bar to pass.
you have a challenge.

Sprawling, verdant grasslands blanketed with daisies, enclosed by majestic pines, standing tall against the barrage of time, while a brook babbled softly in the background, did about as much for him revelation-wise as a half-eaten day-old curry from the Klatchian takeaway next door. The ongoing skirmish between Lord Vetinari and the Times’ crossword compiler is well known, at least from Making Money onwards. title: The Road Between Worlds
author: cookxenya
summary:
Enid and Sue fall through a Thin Place into Valdemar, where nothing behaves the way either of them expects. Sue’s long‑buried Annunaki heritage wakes up, Kyrith claims her as a Seed‑Self, and the Collegium suddenly finds itself hosting a girl who can accidentally reshape the Pattern if she panics.
Then Rincewind arrives. Then Granny Weatherwax arrives. And Valdemar’s polite stability begins to fray.
As Sue learns to ground her Gifts, Enid clings to her Fortress‑Mind explanations, the Herald‑Mages spiral into moral panic, and Granny cuts through everyone’s illusions with surgical precision. When Sue finally explains the Road Between Worlds—the Ledger, the Crucible, the Kinder Contract—the Heralds must confront a philosophy that treats “monsters” as citizens with jobs instead of enemies to be purified.
A multiversal ethics story featuring culture clash, mythic awakening, Discworld pragmatism, Valdemaran idealism, and one very hungry Wraith.

When Sue and her Valdemaran Companion, Kyrith, thump into existence on the deck of the Hunger’s End, they find a universe that doesn't want a savior—it wants a battery. Elder Kaelum, a Perpetual Herald driven to madness by the grim-darkness of the 40k sector, intends to force Sue’s "bloom" to anchor his fleet, even if it means cannibalizing her soul.
Caught in a portable fortress (otherwise known as the Luggage) and struggling with the crushing weight of Christian guilt and Author Knowledge, Sue must decide if she's willing to break every rule to save a single refugee and a broken stallion. From the rust of the Gloop-vats to the crystalline majesty of the Chakram Verita, this is the story of a Seed-self finding her Will.

summary:
"I am the Anchor of Reality. And you are a scrap of discarded thought."
When a transition through the Klein Bottles goes violently wrong, Sue and Kurj Skolia’s elite squadron find themselves stranded in the grim darkness of the 31st Millennium. They haven't just traveled through space; they've overshot their timeline by an epoch, landing in the middle of the Horus Heresy.
For Sue, a Perpetual and Queen of the Great Road, the loss of the trail home is a devastating blow. But for the twenty mortal Skolian pilots under her protection, it's a death sentence—unless she can find a way to make this cruel universe respect her Pattern.
From dismantling Greater Daemons with hard-light whips to stabilizing the Astronomican at the foot of the Golden Throne, Sue must navigate the politics of a paranoid Emperor and the tragedy of Magnus the Red. She isn't just surviving; she’s forging a new Warrant for a world that has never known peace.

summary:
Minnie Perkins is having a bad day. She’s "under the weather" (literally), crying "rivers of sorrow" (with actual trout), and the more she speaks, the more reality breaks.
On Discworld, Granny Weatherwax tries to anchor the girl to common sense. In the 500 Kingdoms, Godmother Elena is forcibly summoned by a Tradition desperate to script the chaos. From Xanth, a trickster nudges the puns toward a total reality collapse. The resulting fracture acts as a beacon for the 40k Warp, threatening a catastrophic collision of grim-dark proportions.
Enter Sue, a Primaris-Superior Empress-in-Waiting, riding the Companion Stallion Kyrith. With a Spirit Cube in hand and the authority of the Moirae behind her, she arrives to ground the Warp... A story about language discipline, headology, and Narrative Causality.

title: Storm Threads
author: cookxenya
summary: When Haven One collapses into a Warhammer-infested reality, Sue executes a surgical extraction—shielding survivors, salvaging archives, and misleading Ork warbands with psychological decoys. As the multiversal storm spreads, she stabilizes three more displaced Havens, threading emotional logic into terrain, Groves, and Companion births. She holds the Knot—a recursive tangle seeded by the Fates—by anchoring grief, guilt, pride, and silence into resonance. Her recovery is quiet, her leadership sovereign. She trains a mixed-Gift class in a destabilized hall, teaching clarity over doctrine. When the Monarchs convene, she reframes their summit as triage. No merger, no throne—just a framework that holds contradiction long enough to matter. The Grove resumes, recalibrated to birth Companions tuned to survival, not tradition.

summary:
Sue’s assignment to Commander Kurj Skolia’s highly secure command deck is a cruel irony. She protested the posting, citing her 'untestable' power and the overwhelming, inexplicable pull she feels toward him. Now, forced to serve as a page, her simple mission to observe is complicated by a desperate battle for control.
Every humming console amplifies her fear, and she struggles to conceal the latent Gifts—foresight, empathy, and mage-sense—that constantly threaten to expose her. Her only anchor against the panic is the quiet pulse of her Companion, Kyrith.
Kurj, the imposing Emperor, is acutely aware of the unique resonance of her tightly folded power, sensing the untestable currents she tries to hide. When he actively tests her control, forcing her to instinctively correct a deck malfunction, Sue realizes she is no longer an invisible beginner. Kurj sees her, and his intense focus means her life—and the fate of the command deck—will never be the same.
The struggle for meaning has begun.

Their bond deepens as they navigate a refugee Cube, and Sue’s identity as an avatar of the Heart is confirmed.
Through Median trials, she undergoes nanosurgery and VRCL upgrades, mastering her Gifts and aligning her instincts. She trains in the Three Courts, stabilizes fractured universes, and integrates vampires into multiversal governance. With Kurj, Kyrith, and the Runabout’s Companion, she returns to the Road, installs shrine nodes, and deploys memetic infrastructure.
When Kurj’s homeworld is threatened by Rift-born demons, Sue leads the defense—coordinating fleets, deploying avatars, and anchoring emotional resonance. Her Whatsits, Courts, and allies work in harmony. By the end, she is no longer surviving—she is governing, healing, and shaping the multiverse itself.

Juliet Stollop, meanwhile, is more concerned with shoes, sugar buns, and her newfound role in the “glamour of foot-the-ball.”
When a chance meeting at Unseen University sets them on an unexpected path, Carrot and Juliet stumble into the strangest kind of courtship—one where civic duty looks suspiciously like romance, football rules are explained with pastries, and dinner dates are mistaken for safety patrols.
With Glenda and Nobby providing running commentary, and half the Watch placing bets, Ankh-Morpork gains a new odd couple: the tall watchman who salutes everyone, and the night kitchen girl who thinks cabbage is romantic.

title: Footnotes and Forgery

summary:
When a shipment of gold vanishes in Ankh-Morpork, Moist von Lipwig finds himself accused—naturally. To his horror (and Carrot’s delight), Lord Vetinari pairs them together to recover the missing fortune.
Moist relies on cons, scams, and quick talking; Carrot relies on honesty, sincerity, and the unnerving ability to make hardened criminals feel guilty. Between bungled escape attempts, creative bookkeeping corrected with cheerful footnotes, and thieves who surrender after being asked politely, the two men discover that opposites don’t just attract—they confound, exasperate, and, eventually, kiss.
A story of scams undone by sincerity, footnotes that ruin forgeries, and the uncomfortable truth that some partnerships can’t be escaped, no matter how many times you try to slip out the back door.
